steps.prompt: Before the check: which part of this unit feels easiest, and which do you want to look at again?

cards.title: Direct speech: quick review
cards.body: Exact words go in quotation marks. Tag first: Ana said, “Let’s go.” Tag last: “Let’s go,” Ana said. Split: “If we hurry,” said Ana, “we’ll make it.” Commas and end marks go inside, the quote starts with a capital, and every new speaker gets a new line.

cards.title: Reported speech: quick review
cards.body: No quotation marks. Change the pronouns, shift the verb back (is → was, will → would), and shift time and place words (tomorrow → the next day, here → there). Questions use if/whether or a question word, statement order and a full stop. Commands use told/asked + the person + (not) to + the verb.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll write a short news story that shows off everything you’ve learned. Quill gives it a score.

prompts: What did you learn about direct and reported speech that you didn’t know before this unit?
In your next essay, how will you decide whether to quote or to report what a source says?
